requirements.text: Pipeup adds one control to the page, flush with the bottom-right corner of the window, and nothing else; the page's own layout, look and behaviour outside comment mode stay exactly as the author made them.

In comment mode, hovering outlines the most obvious block under the pointer and names it by what it is and its own words, with the choices to move the comment around it, inside it, or to a pin, and clicking a block opens the comment box at once.

Anyone can write a comment without giving a name, in plain text with line breaks and links, beside the block it is about; typed words are never lost unless the reviewer cancels, and then Undo is offered.

Every thread shows as the same compact card wherever it appears: the writer, how long ago, the words and the reply count, with its actions on hover; on documents the cards sit in a column beside the content, level with what they are about, and open with a reply box.

The comment control's menu offers Copy comments as Markdown and as text; the Markdown says, for every open thread, where it is (section, element, quoted words or pin), who wrote it and when, and the comment and its replies, and a message beside the control confirms the copy.
When the clipboard cannot be written, the text to copy is selected on the page and the message says which key finishes the copy, as the person's keyboard labels it.

In comment mode, selecting words offers one comment icon just past the end of the paragraph's text, level with the selection's last line, never covering the words; pressing it opens the comment box for exactly those words, which then carry a soft highlight that opens the thread.

In comment mode, Option-click (or the naming bar's Pin, or on touch screens Pin then a tap) drops a pin at an exact spot and opens the comment box at once; the pin keeps its position relative to its element, shows its thread's number once sent, and opens its thread beside it.

Every thread takes replies one level deep beneath the comment, reactions as a quick row of five emoji that become counted pills, and a More menu with Copy thread, and on the writer's own comment Edit and Delete, where Delete asks once more.

All comments lists every thread in page order with the words it is about, filters it to mentions and to resolved threads, opens each thread in place and reveals where it is on the page, and the page moves over so the panel covers nothing.

A reviewer can add or change their name in place on the menu's first row (and on the compose card), with Enter or leaving the field saving and Esc cancelling, and the name shows on every card and in every copy.
Cancel or Esc throws a comment's words away only with a message beside the control that offers Undo for a few seconds (also ⌘Z or Ctrl+Z), which brings the box back with the words in it.
Deleting a comment asks once more in a dialog that says what goes with it; a deleted comment leaves nothing in its place, and deleting a thread's first comment removes the whole thread.
Resolve takes a thread and its mark off the page and out of every copy, with a message beside the control; the thread stays reachable in All comments with Resolved on, where Reopen brings it back.
With Resolved on, All comments lists resolved threads among the open ones, muted and marked resolved, each with Reopen.
On a deck, Pipeup follows the deck's own controls and never blocks turning a slide, in comment mode too, and its control counts only the current slide's open threads.
A pin dropped on a slide belongs to that slide, keeps its position relative to the slide when it is resized, and is numbered among that slide's threads.
Only the current slide's threads show; the control counts them, and a mark on it with its label say how many threads other slides hold.
On a deck, All comments groups threads by slide in deck order with the current slide marked, and choosing a thread turns the deck to its slide.
Threads from several reviewers show side by side, each signed with its writer's name and avatar, and an author may edit or delete only their own comments.
The copied Markdown names the writer and time of every comment and reply, and the author's page offers one prompt that carries it to a coding agent.
On a touch screen the control is at least 44 px square, every tap Pipeup answers works the first time, and the menu opens and closes by tap alone.
Comments, the reviewer's name, the theme and the hidden choice are kept for a page in the browser it was reviewed in, and come back when the page is reopened.
An author adds Pipeup with one pinned script tag and one document key, both copied whole from one page, and the key is made once and kept.
Hide comments puts every card, highlight and pin out of sight until it is turned off, while the control still counts the open threads, and the choice is kept for the page in that browser.
A thread whose content is gone from the page stays listed and counted in All comments, marked as content gone with where it was, and is never dropped or attached to the wrong place.
The check reports, at three widths, what Pipeup would change or cover on a page, names the fix, and says when the page is ready to review.

On a touch screen one tap picks a block and opens the box at once, long-press selects words with the comment icon at the screen's edge, and the box and its buttons always sit in the part of the screen the keyboard leaves.
On a narrow screen All comments takes the full width, the page waits beneath it, and each open card keeps the words it is about.

steps.name: Add the script tag and the key

criteria.text: Given the page, when Tom presses Copy on the script block, then the clipboard holds exactly the script tag with its pinned version and integrity, and the button reads "Copied".
Given the page, when it is read, then it offers exactly two things to copy, the key attribute and the script tag, and one way to make a key.

steps.name: Run the check

criteria.text: Given the command, when Tom presses Copy, then the clipboard holds exactly the command with no prompt.
Given a page that passes, when the report renders, then it lists 390, 820 and 1280 each with "nothing covered, nothing changed" and ends "ready to review".
Given a page whose footer link the tag covers at 1280, when the report renders, then it names the link and the fix.

steps.name: See every reviewer's comments on the page

criteria.text: Given five threads by three writers, when the page renders, then each card shows its writer's name and the tag reads 4.
Given a thread by Red Fox, when Tom opens its More menu, then it offers Copy thread only.

steps.name: Hand the comments to an agent

criteria.text: Given four threads by three writers, when Tom copies as Markdown, then the clipboard names Maya Lindqvist, Red Fox and Otter on their comments and the message reads "Copied 4 comments as Markdown."
Given the prompt card, when he presses Copy prompt, then the clipboard holds "Work through each thread below and say what changed." followed by the Markdown.

journeys.title: Come back to a page later

steps.name: Reopen the page with its comments

criteria.text: Given three threads made earlier, when the page is reopened in the same browser, then the three cards, the highlight and the pin are back and the tag reads 3.
Given a name given earlier, when the page is reopened, then every card shows it.

steps.name: Hide the comments to read

criteria.text: Given three threads showing, when Maya turns on Hide comments, then no card, highlight or pin shows and the tag still reads 3.
Given comments hidden, when she reopens the page, then they are still hidden and the menu row reads On.

steps.name: Find a thread whose words were cut

criteria.text: Given a thread on a paragraph that was cut, when Maya opens All comments, then the thread is listed with "Content gone · was in The river" and the tag counts it.
Given that thread, when she copies as Markdown, then the text holds it with where it was.

steps.name: See every comment in one place

criteria.text: Given three threads, when Maya opens All comments, then a panel on the right lists the three in page order, each with the words it is about, and the page's content is narrower but all still visible.
Given the panel open, when she chooses the second card, then it opens out in place with its reply box and the page scrolls to its paragraph.
Given the panel open, when she turns on For you, then the list reads "No comments mention you", and turning it off brings the three back.
Given the panel open, when she presses Esc, then the panel closes and focus is on the comment control.

steps.name: Bring resolved threads back

criteria.text: Given one resolved thread and the panel open, when Maya turns on Resolved, then the list shows four threads in page order with the resolved one marked "· resolved" and offering Reopen.
criteria.setup: the all-comments screen, then Resolve on the pin thread.

criteria.text: Given Resolved on, when she turns it off, then the resolved thread leaves the list and the open three remain.

steps.name: Reply, react, or change your mind

criteria.text: Given her thread open, when Maya types a reply and presses Enter, then the reply appears indented beneath the comment with her name and "just now", and the reply box is empty with focus still in it.
Given her thread open, when she presses React and chooses 👍, then "👍 1" shows under the comment and the quick row goes.
Given her thread open, when she presses More, then a menu shows Copy thread, Edit and Delete in that order, and Esc closes it with focus back on More.
Given the More menu open, when she chooses Delete and confirms, then the thread and its card are gone and the tag's count falls by one.

steps.name: Delete a comment, asked once more

criteria.text: Given her thread open, when Maya chooses Delete in the More menu, then a dialog asks "Delete this comment?" and says it has no replies, with Cancel focused.
Given the dialog, when she presses Esc, then it closes, the thread is still there and focus is on More.
Given the dialog, when she presses Delete, then the card is gone, no mark is left beside the paragraph and the tag shows no count.

steps.name: Resolve a thread, and bring it back

criteria.text: Given her thread at rest, when Maya presses Resolve, then the card and the paragraph's mark are gone, the tag's count falls by one and "Resolved." shows beside the tag.
Given a resolved thread, when she copies as Markdown, then the thread is not in the text.
Given a resolved thread and All comments open with Resolved on, when she presses Reopen on it, then the card is back beside its paragraph and the tag's count rises by one.
criteria.setup: the read-thread screen, Esc, then Resolve; then All comments with Resolved on.

steps.name: Open the page

criteria.text: Given the report opened from disk with Pipeup in it, when the page renders, then the only thing of Pipeup's on screen is the 32 px tag in the bottom-right corner, and every element of the author's page keeps its size, place and style.
Given the page open, when Maya points at the tag, then its shortcut slides out to the left and the tag stays where it was.

steps.name: Pick a block to comment on

criteria.text: Given comment mode on, when Maya moves the pointer over the second paragraph, then a dashed outline surrounds that paragraph without changing its size or place, and the bar above it reads "Paragraph · We recommend raising the deck".
Given a block outlined, when Maya clicks it, then the comment box opens with the cursor in it, with no second click.

Given the second paragraph picked with words typed, when Maya presses Around it, then the comment box moves to the section The river with the words kept, and a second press moves it to the page as a whole.
Given comment mode on, when Maya presses Esc, then comment mode ends, the outline and bar fade out and the page behaves as normal.

steps.name: Write the comment

criteria.text: Given the comment box open and empty, when Maya looks at it, then it shows who she is with a way to change her name, the placeholder "Comment or add others with @", and a greyed Comment button.
Given words typed in the box, when Maya clicks on the page's blank space, then the box and its words stay where they are.
Given words typed, when Maya presses Enter, then the comment is sent and the box becomes a thread in the same place.

steps.name: Read it back beside the text

criteria.text: Given a comment just sent on the second paragraph, when the page is looked at, then a card with Maya's name, "just now" and her words sits in the column level with that paragraph, open, with the cursor in its reply box, and the corner tag reads 1.
Given the open card, when Maya presses Esc, then the card closes to its compact form and focus returns to the paragraph's highlight.
Given the compact card, when Maya points at it, then React, Resolve and More fade in at its top right and nothing on the card moves.

steps.name: Comment on a few words

criteria.text: Given comment mode on, when Maya selects "rose twice that week" in the first paragraph, then one comment icon appears just past the end of that paragraph's text, level with the selection's last line, and no block outline shows.
Given the icon showing, when she presses it and types, then the comment box opens in the column level with the paragraph and the selected words stay marked.
Given comment mode off, when she selects words, then nothing of Pipeup's is offered.

steps.name: Drop a pin on an exact spot

criteria.text: Given comment mode on, when Maya Option-clicks just under "The path", then a pin appears at that spot, open, and the comment box opens in the column level with it with the cursor in it.
Given a pin's comment sent, when she looks at the page, then the pin shows 3 and the corner tag reads 3.
Given the pin, when the window is resized, then the pin keeps its place relative to the heading it sits under.

steps.name: Copy every comment as Markdown

criteria.text: Given the tag outside comment mode, when Maya clicks it, then the menu rises above the tag with who she is, Copy comments, Theme, All comments · 3, Hide comments and Start commenting with its shortcut, in that order.

Given the menu open, when Maya chooses Copy comments then As Markdown, then the clipboard holds Markdown that names the section, the element and the quoted words or the pin of each of her three threads, her name and time, and her words, and the message "Copied 3 comments as Markdown." shows beside the tag.
Given one of the three threads resolved, when she copies as Markdown, then only the two open threads are in the text and the count says 2.
criteria.setup: the pin thread resolved from its card.

steps.name: The clipboard is blocked

criteria.text: Given a browser that refuses clipboard writes, when Maya chooses As Markdown, then the Markdown appears selected in a block beside the page and a message beside the tag names the copy key for her platform.
criteria.setup: the browser's clipboard permission denied for the page.

criteria.text: Given the text selected, when she presses the named key, then the clipboard holds the same Markdown and the message reads "Copied 3 comments as Markdown."

steps.name: Undo a cancelled comment

criteria.text: Given words typed in the comment box, when Maya presses Esc, then the box goes and a message beside the tag reads "Comment discarded." with Undo.
Given the message showing, when she presses Undo, then the box is back in the same place with the same words and the cursor at their end.
Given the message showing, when a few seconds pass, then the message and its Undo are gone.
criteria.setup: the write-comment screen, words typed, then Esc.

steps.name: Open the deck

criteria.text: Given the deck opened, when the page renders, then slide 1 of 3 shows with the deck's own Previous, Next and count, and the only thing of Pipeup's is the tag in the corner.
Given comment mode on, when Maya presses Next, then slide 2 shows and comment mode is still on.

steps.name: Drop a pin on a slide

criteria.text: Given slide 2 in comment mode, when Maya Option-clicks the slide, then a pin appears on it, open, and the comment box opens beside the slide with the cursor in it.
Given the box with words, when she presses Enter, then the pin reads 1 and the tag reads 1.

steps.name: Turn to the next slide

criteria.text: Given two threads on slide 2, when Maya presses Next, then slide 3 shows no pin and no card, and the tag shows its mark with the label "0 here · 2 on other slides".
Given slide 3, when she presses Previous, then slide 2's two pins and cards are back and the tag reads 2.

steps.name: See every comment grouped by slide

criteria.text: Given threads on slides 2 and 3, when Maya opens All comments on slide 2, then the list shows "Slide 2 · 2 open" marked as this slide, then "Slide 3 · 1 open", each with its threads.
Given the panel, when she chooses the slide 3 thread, then the deck turns to slide 3 and that thread opens in the panel.

steps.name: Open the page on a phone

criteria.text: Given a 390 × 844 touch screen, when the page renders, then the page never scrolls sideways, the tag is at least 44 px square at the bottom-right corner, and nothing else of Pipeup's shows.
Given the tag, when Maya taps it, then the menu opens above it and fits in the screen.

steps.name: Tap a block and type

criteria.text: Given comment mode on a 390 × 844 touch screen, when Maya taps the second paragraph, then it is outlined and the comment box opens below it with the cursor in it, and no second tap is needed.
Given the box with words, when she presses Enter, then the thread sits below the paragraph and the page never scrolls sideways.

steps.name: See every comment full width

criteria.text: Given three threads on a 390 × 844 screen, when Maya opens All comments, then the panel is as wide as the screen, the page is not visible beside it, and the three cards show with the words they are about.
Given the panel, when she presses Close, then the page is back and the tag is in its corner.

steps.name: Add your name

criteria.text: Given the menu open, when Maya chooses the edit mark, then the first row becomes a text field holding her current name with the cursor at its end, and the menu stays open.
Given the field, when she types a name and presses Enter, then the row shows that name with the edit mark, and every card on the page shows it.
Given the field, when she presses Esc, then the row shows the name she had and the menu is still open.
